chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever causes an incident in Medina or shelters an incident-maker, upon him is the Curse of Allah.' I said, 'And what is the incident?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The killing.'

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: caused an incident / did something new
key_terms.مُحْدِثاً: one who causes an incident / the perpetrator

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'hadath' (incident) in the context of Medina's sanctity according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the 'newly invented matter' (hadath) triggering Allah's curse refers specifically to homicide, thereby linking the sanctity of Medina to the preservation of life. This definition underscores the gravity of shedding blood within the Prophet's city, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the inviolability of Medina's airspace and streets. The hadith serves as a foundational text for understanding the spiritual and legal consequences of violence in this sacred locale.
